To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rheumatoid synovium contains a population of T cells with an intermediate phenotype of activation, which may represent a subset of T cells activated or reactivated within the synovium.

dual CD45RA and CD45RO positive lymphocytes are found within synovial tissue from rheumatoid arthritis patients, but not from osteoarthritic synovium, and that the frequency of these lymphocytes in rheumatoid synovial fluid is greater than that in peripheral blood.
dual CD45RA and CD45RO positive cells are found in the synovium and fluid of patients with rheumatoid arthritis, but not in the fluid of osteoarthritis patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the mechanisms involved in the initiation and maintenance of the immune response in rheumatoid arthritis.
the study of the immunology of the rheumatoid synovium, and the identification of the cells responsible for the inflammatory process.
the identification of the cellular and molecular mechanisms involved in the initiation and perpetuation of the autoimmune process in rheumatoid arthritis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovium is infiltrated with a large proportion of CD45RA+CD45RO+ T cells, and that this is not a feature of the normal synovium.

the presence of dual CD45 positive T cells in the rheumatoids joints is not due to an expansion of a particular T cell population, but rather to a change in phenotype from CD45RO positive to CD45RA positive.

the presence of a large proportion of dual CD45 RA, CD45RO T cells in the rheumatoids joint is associated with a lack or reduced expression of early activation antigena nd a high expression of HLA class II antigens, suggesting that the cells may be activated within the joint.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dual CD45RA and CD45RO expression is a feature of T cells in rheumatoid synovial tissues.
the rheumatoid synovium is an immunologically active site, which may be responsible for the local production of immunoregulatory cytokines.
dual CD45RA and CD45RO positive cells are present in PB, SF and synovium of rheumatoid patients, and are increased in SF and synovial tissue compared with PB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD45RA and CD45RO expression is a useful marker for the identification of T cells in RA.
the CD45RA,CD45RO double‐positive phenotype is not a marker of recent thymic emigration, as previously suggested, but rather a marker of T cell activation in the rheumatologic diseases.
the dual CD45RO, CD45RA positive T cell phenotype is not restricted to the rheumatoid arthritis joint.
